title: A Landfall for the Escarpment
premise: Yara Crane, a storm chaser deep in debt to the Vellum Syndicate, is sent upriver to find a missing survey expedition — not to rescue them, but to recover the land deed they carry, proof of inheritance that would bankrupt his creditors. He finds one survivor, Ilse Marchetti, who knows the deed names her, and together they flee across the Escarpment ahead of the early snows, hunted by syndicate men and betrayed by the guide Yara trusted. In the end Yara burns the debt ledger instead of the deed, choosing justice outside the law over his own survival price, and walks out of the mountains owing nothing but what he can carry.
about_author: Wren Winterbourne is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons on the northern waterways before turning to writing. Their fiction draws on real expeditions gone quiet and the people who go looking for them.

chapters.title: The Debt of Good Weather
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Chasing a storm cell for hire money, he crashes his truck and learns the Vellum Syndicate has bought his debt outright. The emotional beat is dread dressed as bravado: he laughs at the wrong moment and signs away his winter.

chapters.title: A Job Upstream
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The syndicate offers him a way out: find the missing Marchetti survey team upriver and bring back their case documents. He tells himself it's recovery work, not robbery. The beat is self-deception hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: The Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with an intercut of the expedition's final radio log. He replays the garbled last message — 'the escarpment is moving' — and realizes the team wasn't lost to weather alone. Beat: unease becoming certainty.

chapters.title: Hired Hands
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He assembles a small crew: taciturn boatman Odell, young radio tech Pim, and guide Sarel Vance, an old friend whose debts match his own. Beat: camaraderie built on shared desperation, each hiding what they truly want from the trip.

chapters.title: Upriver in Falling Light
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The journey upstream through narrowing gorges; abandoned camps, a burned supply cache, claw marks too deliberate for animals. Beat: the wilderness stops being scenery and becomes a witness.

chapters.title: The Silent Camp
chapters.summary: Sarel's POV. They find the expedition's main camp — tents slashed from inside, instruments arranged in careful rows, no bodies. Sarel recognizes the arrangement as a message meant for someone specific. Beat: horror sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: One Survivor
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They find Ilse Marchetti half-starved in a cave, guarding a metal case. She trusts no one, least of all the man sent by the syndicate — until Yara admits why he came. Beat: hostile honesty forging a fragile alliance.

chapters.title: What the Deed Says
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She reveals the case holds the original land grant: the Escarpment itself, inherited by her family, which the syndicate needs erased to legalize its mining claims. Beat: the stakes invert — she isn't cargo, she's the claim.

chapters.title: Vance's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sarel's POV. Alone at night, Sarel radios the syndicate: he'll deliver the girl and the case if his debt dies with Yara's. Beat: betrayal committed quietly, almost tenderly, because he believes everyone else would do the same.

chapters.title: The First Snow
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Winter arrives weeks early; the river ices over, stranding them. They must cross the range on foot or die waiting. Beat: grief for the easy route, and the first real choice made as a group rather than a contract.

chapters.title: Above the Treeline
chapters.summary: Pim's POV. The climb; Pim's radio catches fragments of syndicate chatter confirming someone aboard is feeding them coordinates. Paranoia spreads. Beat: trust cracking under cold and altitude.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. A blizzard separates the party. Ilse saves Pim's life using survey-team skills, earning the crew's loyalty Yara never could buy. Beat: competence as redemption, and Ilse becoming leader rather than prize.

chapters.title: The Hanging Valley
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Sheltering in a valley of frozen waterfalls, Yara and Ilse trade histories — her family's stolen land, his father's death in a syndicate flood. Beat: two kinds of inheritance, both ruinous, recognized.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Col
chapters.summary: Odell's POV. Syndicate men intercept them at the pass; Odell takes a bullet covering the others' escape and dies naming Sarel as the traitor. Beat: sacrifice without ceremony, rage without a target yet.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Hunted downhill through timberline, Yara confronts Sarel privately. Sarel doesn't deny it — he argues survival is arithmetic. Yara lets him go rather than kill him. Beat: mercy as a wound he gives himself.

chapters.title: Ledger and Land
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Captured briefly by a syndicate scout party, Ilse reads the men their own ledger aloud — every debt, every forged signature — sowing doubt among hired guns who realize they're expendable. Beat: words as weapons; two scouts defect.

chapters.title: The Moving Escarpment
chapters.summary: Pim's POV. The truth of the last transmission: thaw and mining blasts have destabilized the ridge, and the mountain is failing above the syndicate's own camp. Beat: terrible irony — the land collecting its own debt.

chapters.title: Runout
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Racing the slope failure toward the syndicate base where the master ledger is kept, the defected scouts guide them through service tunnels. Beat: momentum, fear, and the strange calm of having stopped calculating odds.

chapters.title: What Burns
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Climax. Confronting syndicate broker Halvorsen in the collapsing base, Yara is offered the deed's destruction in exchange for his freedom. Instead he throws the debt ledger into the fire and keeps the deed intact. Beat: the choice that defines him.

chapters.title: After the Mountain Settles
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Dawn after the slide; the syndicate camp is buried, Halvorsen fled, Sarel found alive and broken among the wreckage. Ilse chooses testimony over vengeance. Beat: exhausted clarity — justice begun, not finished.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The survivors reach the lowlands as the deed goes to the territorial court. Yara owes nothing now except answers, and gives them freely. Beat: lightness earned the hard way.

chapters.title: The Forgiving Ground
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, closing. Spring on the Escarpment: the land granted back, mining halted, Yara leaving on foot with a new storm season ahead. Final beat: the wilderness forgets less than people hope, forgives more than they deserve.
